title: VDBE MakeReady bulk allocation, Parse transfer, and rewind

scope.rationale: MakeReady is the one-way packaging boundary from Parse-owned builder metadata to execution-ready Vdbe arrays. ReusableSpace/allocSpace, Mem initialization, rewind, transferred VList, array/count fields, and execution defaults form one inseparable ownership unit.
excluded_responsibilities: Runtime cursor opening/closing and Mem value destruction
Final Parse destruction and production compiler migration

external_source_responsibilities: Verified Mem/Vdbe/Op layouts and 8-byte allocator alignment
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete active MakeReady, reusable-tail allocator, Mem-array initialization, VList transfer and Rewind state transition are assigned. Runtime teardown and production compiler ownership remain follow-on units.

inputs: INIT Vdbe with at least OP_Init and allocator-reported szOpAlloc
matching Parse sizing/flag metadata with no sticky OOM
outputs: resolved operation metadata, transferred VList, aMem/aVar/apArg/apCsr and counts, optional pFree allocation, READY execution defaults
contracts.ownership: Unused aligned opcode-tail bytes are reused first. One connection allocation owns only unmet array demand through pFree. Parse pVList ownership moves to Vdbe. Array pointers may independently target opcode-tail or pFree storage.
contracts.state_and_results: Cursor cells add to nMem; aMem[0] exists when memory exists without cursors. Explain enforces ten cells and result columns. Mem arrays initialize only flags/db/szMalloc. Rewind sets READY, pc=-1, OK/Abort defaults and counters.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller holds connection mutex. No callback or I/O occurs.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Deficit allocation OOM preserves any tail pointers but publishes zero nVar/nCursor/nMem, retains sticky OOM, and still rewinds to READY for ordinary destruction.

representation_differences: C ReusableSpace uses sqlite3_int64; Zig uses i64 and identical ROUND8/ROUNDDOWN8 arithmetic.
C void-pointer array carving is represented by aligned pointer casts into exact extern layouts.
Parse/Vdbe VList opaque declarations require an ABI-identical pointer cast at ownership transfer.

oracle.protocol: The shared builder worker creates VDBEs then packages normal cursor/variable/argument demand, explain demand, transferred VList ownership, and forced deficit-allocation OOM. C and Zig compare 351 exact observations including arrays, counts, Mem headers, cursor zeroing, pFree, flags, label retirement and rewind state.
internal_observations: array pointer presence and published counts
oracle.normalization: Pointer addresses are normalized to presence, owner transfer, and db identity. Counts, flags, Mem headers, state and OOM results are exact.

assurance.oom: Normal tail-only packaging and forced pFree allocation failure are reached; failed packaging publishes zero executable array counts and remains destructible.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O/callback. Production mutex and runtime cursor lifecycle remain integration obligations.
assurance.malformed_input: Source assertions constrain matching Parse/Vdbe ownership, INIT state, positive opcode count, aligned/nonnegative tail and no entry OOM.
assurance.continuation: READY state after success and allocation failure is observed; transferred and allocated owners are retired between cases.
assurance.performance: Preserves reverse fixup, first-pass tail reuse, one aggregate deficit allocation, second-pass fill and nearby Mem-header initialization.

integration.native_call_path: Symbolic native worker executes Create -> MakeReady on exact Parse/Vdbe/Sqlite3 owners. Handwritten compiler/runtime remain production owners.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No. P4/deletion and compiler/runtime migration remain open.

independent_review.notes: Requires teardown/runtime integration, assurance closure, and independent review.

known_blockers: Port P4 ownership and VDBE operation/object destruction.
Switch compiler/runtime ownership from handwritten Program to source VDBE and retire duplicate representations.
